newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Budapest grain prices fall on expected bumper crop.
newsitem.headline: Budapest grain prices fall on expected bumper crop.

text.p: Grains futures prices on the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) continued to tumble on Tuesday on the back of falling world prices and the prospect of a bumper East European harvest, dealers said.

Milling wheat fell for all months by between 250 and the daily allowed limit of 400 forints while feed wheat and barley also eased for most months. Only December maize rose while November maize was stable.
"The basic idea is that the world market is going down while Eastern Europe will have an extremely large crop this year," said Gabor Herczeg of LaSalle.

The biggest losers were free-falling July 1998 maize which fell 800 forints to 22,100 and October 1997 milling wheat, which dropped 830 to 20,320 forints. August and March feed barley also plummeted by 920 and 800 forints to 18,200 and 20,600 forints, respectively, while December dropped by limit.
Only December maize registered a rise, by 360 to 19,260.
Heczeg predicted further falls in the days to come.
"Provided the world market...doesn't pick up sharply, the Hungarian market will still search for new lows," he said.
Total grains turnover on the BCE was steady at 1,252 lots or 522.66 million forints, compared to Monday's 1,273 lots or 583 million forints.
